topic: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT): The Magic of Convergence

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Normal Distribution
lecture_lines: The Normal Distribution forms a perfect bell curve.
It is defined by its mean and standard deviation.
The shape remains symmetrical around the central peak.
animations: Create a Bell curve on #000000 background.
Highlight the mean at the center with #FF5733.
Shade the area within one standard deviation in #33FF57.

sections.title: The Problem: Randomness in the Wild
lecture_lines: Real-world data is often not normally distributed.
Many distributions are skewed, uniform, or discrete.
We need to predict outcomes despite this randomness.
animations: Show a scatter plot of chaotic data points.
Draw a trend line through the data in #33FFF5.
Display error bars around points in #F533FF.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Sampling Distributions
lecture_lines: Sampling distributions track the average of sample means.
Even non-normal populations produce orderly sample means.
These means gradually cluster into a bell curve.
animations: Generate a population distribution histogram in #FFFFFF.
Show smaller samples being pulled from the population.
Draw the mean of each sample as a dot.
Plot the distribution of these sample means.
Show the sample means converging to a normal curve.

sections.title: The Central Limit Theorem Defined
lecture_lines: The CLT states sample means approach normality.
This occurs regardless of the population distribution shape.
Larger sample sizes yield a more perfect curve.
The distribution always converges toward a normal shape.
This bridge connects random data to normal statistics.
animations: Show the distribution normalizing as sample size increases.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Law of Averages
lecture_lines: The CLT enables powerful statistical hypothesis testing.
Confidence intervals become reliable for unknown populations.
We can predict behavior from irregular data sets.
animations: Show a large set of random events.
Visualize the average of these events stabilizing.
